description.purpose: The round table of the builder's tool loop: one row per turn of one build. `build_id` correlates every row of one wish, `iter` names the round inside it, `role` names what a row is: `user`, `assistant` and `tool` are the loop itself -- and the `user` row is written by `brief`, in the same bundle as the `system` row, because `brief` runs once and every round after the first is assembled from this table (GH #477); a `system` row is not a turn but the instruction tree the build was briefed with, lifted back into the body's system slot on every round that re-enters the composer; `receipt` is a refusal handed back by the submitter, which belongs in the rebuilt thread but is not a tool answer, so no round set counts it; `manifest` is the binding row `normalise` writes when it mints a digest (`manifest_sha256` beside the `build_id`), which is how a later round finds the build a refusal is talking about; and `caller` is the note `weave` parks when the composer opens a round -- who asked, under which tool_call_id, and through which door the answer goes back (`build_caller`, `build_auto_submit`) -- which is how the requester survives a round one of the eyes won (GH #460) and how an operator-initiated build finds the front door again after the same break (GH #480). It is parked whenever the context names any of those keys: an operator has a door and no tool_call_id, and the guard that tested for the id alone left exactly that build without a row. A `caller` row is never a turn, and neither is a `system` row: the first is read back into the header, the second into the body's system slot, and both are skipped when the thread is rebuilt. `turn` is the JSON-serialised UBF turn (or the array of assistant tool-call turns), and `fired` is the compare-and-set guard that grants exactly one weave path permission to cross the re-entry edge.
description.use_when: Beside `weave`, inside the builder hive; written by `brief` once, at the head of a build, and by `weave` for everything after it. Never addressed from outside: the hive is sealed and this cell has no lane of its own.
description.not_in_scope: No retention policy and no pruning: a build is minutes long, not a session. No reading by anything but `weave` -- a second reader would be a second protocol over the same guard, and `brief` only ever writes.
